issues.legal_issue: An unsecured public tax claim does not take priority over a valid mortgage security enforced by a financial corporation.
material_facts: A borrower had mortgaged assets to secure a loan, and the financial corporation took possession of the assets after defaults and invoked its statutory enforcement powers.
The borrower also owed confirmed central excise duty, and the tax authority sought to recover the dues from the mortgaged assets.
The financial corporation's enforcement rights under the governing financial-corporation law had been extended to it, and that law contained an overriding clause.
The tax authority relied on the ability to recover unpaid duty as an arrear of land revenue; the relevant recovery law did not make the tax dues a first charge on the borrower's property.
issues.conclusion: The excise dues did not have priority over the secured mortgage claim. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the common-law doctrine preserved by Article 372 of the Constitution, the Crown's priority applies to unsecured creditors, not to a mortgagee or other secured creditor. A statutory provision creating a first charge can alter that position, but merely allowing tax dues to be recovered as arrears of land revenue does not create such a charge. Statutory rights under the State Financial Corporations Act, including its overriding clause in Section 46B, prevail over inconsistent laws. The Court relied on Dena Bank v. Bhikhabhai Prabhudas Parekh & Co., Bank of Bihar v. State of Bihar, Bank of India v. Siriguppa Sugars & Chemicals Ltd., Builders Supply Corporation v. Union of India, and State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur v. National Iron & Steel Rolling Corporation; it distinguished Macson Marbles Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India because that case did not decide the priority dispute between a secured creditor and an unsecured tax creditor.

rule.if: secured_vs_public_tax_priority_proceeding and valid_mortgage_security and public_tax_claim_is_unsecured and financial_corporation_has_enforcement_right

predicates.secured_vs_public_tax_priority_proceedin: A proceeding concerns which of a secured creditor and a public authority claiming unpaid tax has priority over the same debtor property.
predicates.valid_mortgage_security: The debtor created a valid mortgage over the property to secure a debt.
predicates.public_tax_claim_is_unsecured: The public authority claims unpaid tax but has no rule giving that tax claim a first charge over the property.
predicates.financial_corporation_has_enforcement_ri: The secured creditor is a financial corporation entitled to enforce its statutory rights against the mortgaged property.

issues.definition: When a priority proceeding involves a valid mortgage, an unsecured public tax claim, and a financial corporation entitled to enforce its rights, the secured creditor has priority over the tax claim.

issues.legal_issue: Recovery of central excise dues as arrears of land revenue does not, by itself, create a first charge over the debtor's property.
material_facts: The tax authority sought to recover confirmed central excise dues from property mortgaged to a financial corporation.
The applicable recovery provision allowed recovery from excisable goods and, if the amount remained unpaid, permitted recovery as an arrear of land revenue.
The tax authority's reliance on the land-revenue recovery procedure was not supported by a provision making the dues a first charge on the debtor's property.
issues.conclusion: The land-revenue recovery procedure did not give the excise dues priority over the mortgage security.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Central Excise Act, 1944, provides for recovery from money owing to the debtor or by attachment and sale of excisable goods, with resort to recovery as an arrear of land revenue if the amount is not recovered that way. That recovery mechanism does not itself convert the tax debt into a first charge on the debtor's property. The Court's approach is consistent with Builders Supply Corporation v. Union of India, which held that recovery as an arrear of land revenue does not, without more, establish priority for tax dues.

predicates.excise_tax_recovery_proceeding: A proceeding concerns collection of unpaid excise tax from a debtor's property.
predicates.recovery_as_land_revenue_is_authorized: The applicable recovery process permits unpaid tax to be collected as an arrear of land revenue after other specified recovery methods do not satisfy it.
predicates.no_first_charge_is_created: No applicable rule expressly makes the tax debt a first charge over the debtor's property.

issues.definition: When an excise-tax recovery proceeding permits collection as land revenue but creates no first charge, that recovery method does not create a first charge.
